newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson sees steady property prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Henderson sees steady property prices rise.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd's chairman Lee Shau Kee said on Tuesday he expected the property market to remain active in Hong Kong but residential prices to rise in line with the inflation.
"I believe that the property market will continue to be active," Lee said after the group's annual general meeting.
"However, a repetition of a sharp 20 or 30 percent (price) rise, which happened in the past, is unlikely because current prices are already at a reasonable level."
"We expect prices to edge up at a steady pace even after 1997, a pace more or less in line with inflation and depending on the condition of supply and demand in the market," he said.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese sovereignty next July 1.
The Consumer Price Index (A), Hong Kong's broadest measure of inflation, rose 5.2 percent on the year in September.
Lee also said in the group's annual report that Hong Kong residential property remains promising due to limited housing supply and growing housing demand.
